subject.title: [Bug]: Secret provider crash-loop exhausts 1Password service account rate limits

question: What startup SecretRef failure policy should OpenClaw own for exec-backed external secret providers under supervisor restart loops?
rationale: The code path is clear, but choosing between fail-fast security, bounded retry/backoff, degraded startup, circuit breaking, and provider-specific rate-limit handling changes operator semantics and security posture.

options.title: Define bounded core startup policy
options.body: Add a generic bounded startup retry/backoff or circuit policy for active SecretRef failures, with operator-visible logs/docs and no 1Password-specific core behavior unless a generic contract requires it.

options.title: Keep fail-fast and document mitigation
options.body: Preserve the current fail-closed startup contract and document supervisor start limits plus external caching/batching resolver plugins such as Varlock for rate-limit-sensitive deployments.

options.title: Adopt provider-specific handling
options.body: Add 1Password/op-specific rate-limit behavior in core, accepting a larger plugin-boundary exception and stronger maintenance burden.

recommendation.title: Define bounded core startup policy
recommendation.body: Add a generic bounded startup retry/backoff or circuit policy for active SecretRef failures, with operator-visible logs/docs and no 1Password-specific core behavior unless a generic contract requires it.

likelyOwner.reason: Josh introduced the SecretRef resolver/runtime shape and is the strongest history signal for the affected core secrets contract.
